Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
curated_comment: Verified against Schmalz 2013:204 (ex.524a 'mit-ek'=1PL.FOC.ABS) and the alignment summary pp.247-248 (Tables 4.2.1, 4.2.4). Value 1 confirmed. Under focus the 1st person pronoun is ergatively aligned: S=O=metek (absolutive -ek) vs A=met (zero/ergative). CAVEAT: focus-conditioned ('pragmatic ergativity', Schmalz); accusative alignment (S=A=met, O=metul/metqane) when S not focused.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?
curated_comment: Verified against Schmalz 2013:168 (ex.405 'tet-ek') and Tables 4.2.1/4.2.4. Value 1 confirmed. 2nd person parallel to 1st: S=O=tetek vs A=tet under focus (ergative); accusative when S not focused. Focus-conditioned (pragmatic ergativity).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on third person pronouns?
curated_comment: CORRECTED 1 -> 0. Directly contradicted by Schmalz's own summary, Schmalz 2013:247-248 (Tables 4.2.2, 4.2.4): 3rd person pronouns have NEUTRAL alignment under focus (S=A=O=tudel/tittel) and neutral or ACCUSATIVE alignment otherwise (O=tudeYane when A is 3rd). Schmalz: 3rd person pronouns 'disrupt the pragmatically triggered regular alternation between accusative and ergative alignment' and never pattern S=O!=A; they cannot take the absolutive -ek/-ley. Hence NO ergative alignment on 3rd person pronouns. The cited p.304 does not support an ergative 3rd person pronoun. Final value set to 0.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
curated_comment: Verified against Schmalz 2013:81-82 and Table 4.2.3/4.2.4 (3rd person NOMINAL). Value 1 confirmed. Under focus, full NPs are ergatively aligned: S=O=ileley (absolutive) vs A=ile (zero/ergative). Focus-conditioned (pragmatic ergativity); accusative when S not focused.
